OpenStrand Studio · feature concept

Stylize End Side

Right-click a layer that has a free end (the green strip on its button) and shape that end however you want: a slanted cut, a rounded tip, a point, a notch, or a longer or shorter end. The strand's body, its side line, its shadow, and any mask that touches that area all follow the same new edge.

Concept only, no app code changed. Every picture of a strand below is drawn by the app's real Strand class with the proposed geometry running on top of it.
Where it livesThe dialogEnd shapesOne profile, four layersWhat moves togetherData & wordingRules & edge casesImplementation map

Where it lives

A free end is an end with no attachment: has_circles[side] is false. The layer panel already shows this as the green strip on the layer button (NumberedLayerButton.paintEvent, colour #3BA424): a strip means at least one end of that layer is free.

The normal right-click menu of that button gains one row, built exactly like the existing Line / Arrow / Dash / Circle rows: a label on the left and one flat button per free end on the right. It sits directly under Close the Knot, the other free-end feature, so the two free-end actions live together.

When the row appears. Regular strand: one button per end whose has_circles is false. Attached strand: only End (its start is glued to the parent, same rule as the Line row). Masked layer: never (masks have no ends of their own). Hidden or locked layers: same as the Line row today, the row is still offered.

The dialog

Modal, one end at a time, and it follows the WidthConfigDialog pattern: translated strings, theme stylesheet, Hebrew right-to-left, hand-built OK / Cancel buttons. Every control is one the app already has: the toggles are the Create Mask Grid dialog's large blue checkbox (proxy-styled 20 px indicator, white tick), the sliders are the Move Group dialog's rows (label, slider, value, text field), and the plus / minus steppers are the segmented [ − | value | + ] spin box from the Settings dialog. The mockups below are built with those exact helpers, not lookalikes. What it adds is the live preview on the canvas that the shadow editor already uses: every change is applied to the strand immediately, so you judge the end in place, next to its shadows and masks. Cancel restores the snapshot taken when the dialog opened. OK pushes one undo step.

Does the Side Line section collide with the rest of the menu?

Checked against every entry of today's right-click menu (show_context_menu) and against how the side line is actually painted (Strand.draw, pen = stroke_color, width = stroke_width). Nothing in the menu owns the side line's colour or thickness today, so the new controls add state rather than fight over it. The rules that keep them consistent:

Existing actionWhat it does to the side line todayWith the new controls
Line row · Show / Hide Start / End LineToggles start_line_visible / end_line_visible.Identical flag as Show side line. Toggle it in either place and the other follows. No second flag is introduced.
Change Stroke Color (set-wide and This Layer Only)_apply_stroke_color sets stroke_color; the side line follows because it is painted with that colour. Circle stroke colours are also overwritten unless they were deliberately made transparent.With Use stroke color ticked (the default) the side line keeps following, exactly as today. With it unticked the pinned colour survives a stroke change, mirroring how a deliberately transparent circle survives. Ticking the box again re-links it. Nothing else in _apply_stroke_color needs to change.
Change Width (both variants)Sets width and stroke_width; the side line thickness follows stroke_width.A thickness left at its default (stored as None) keeps following stroke_width. A thickness set in the dialog is stored as a number and survives the width change. The cap's outline is then that thickness while the long edges stay at stroke_width (the fill is inset by the side-line thickness along the profile and by the stroke width elsewhere).
Change Color (both variants)set_color writes side_line_color = stroke_color, a value nothing reads.That dead sync is removed; side_line_color becomes the pinned colour (None = follow stroke). Fill colour changes never touched the side line and still do not.
Unfold Start Edge, Transparent Closing Knot Side, Restore …Set a circle stroke colour to transparent / back. They act on attached or closed ends, which draw a circle instead of a side line.No overlap: the new row only exists for free ends, and a circle cap always wins over an end style (the style goes dormant, see Rules).
Close the KnotMakes the free end a closed junction (has_circles true).The end style and the side-line settings go dormant with it, and come back if the knot is reopened. Same behaviour end_line_visible has today.
Hide Layer, Shadow Only, Hide Shadow, Edit ShadowsVisibility and shadow flags read in the draw bodies.Unchanged. A shadow-only layer casts the styled shadow; a hidden layer casts none; shadow editor rows are per-layer pairs and do not care about the end.
Arrow / Dash rows, Show Full Arrow and its panelDecorations anchored on the endpoint.They anchor on the profile's farthest point instead (see What moves together); their colours and sizes are their own and stay untouched.
Change Width (This Layer Only) · Match connected strandElliptical caps at junction ends.Junction ends only; free ends only for this feature. The two never apply to the same end.

One thing this audit changed in the design: the side-line thickness now defines the outline thickness of the cap, and the long edges keep the stroke width. Earlier the band was simply the inset ring, which would have made a thicker side line paint over the fill instead of pushing it back.

End shapes

Every shape is one profile: the line the end edge follows across the strand's width. Tilt rotates it, Depth scales it, Extend / Trim slides it. All twelve ends below are the same strand, rendered by the geometry prototype on top of the real Strand.

ShapeProfile across the width (local frame)Depth means
StraightA line square to the strand. Sits at x = stroke_width, exactly where today's side line ends.—
AngledThe same line, rotated by Tilt around the endpoint. The cut is stretched so it still spans the full width (a 45° cut is √2 longer than the strand is wide).—
RoundedA half-ellipse bulging outward: full width across, Depth × half-width deep. 100 % is a true round cap.Roundness
PointedTwo straight segments meeting on the centreline, Depth × width ahead of the edge.Tip length
NotchedPointed, mirrored inward: a V cut into the strand.Notch depth
ConcaveRounded, mirrored inward: a scooped end.Hollow depth

One profile, four layers

Today a free end is a flat cap: the body is the centre curve stroked with Qt.FlatCap (fill at width, stroke at width + 2·stroke_width), and the side line is a separate stroke_width-thick line drawn just past the endpoint, across the full width (update_side_line, then painter.drawLine). Shadows stroke the same centre curve with the same flat cap, and masks intersect the same stroked paths. Four independent pieces of code agree only because they all happen to say FlatCap.

The proposal replaces that coincidence with one rule. In the local frame of the end (origin at the endpoint, x pointing outward along the curve's tangent, y across the width) the style defines a profile P(y). Everything else is derived from it:

  1. Outer footprint. Take the flat-capped stroke path, subtract everything beyond the profile, and add the region between the endpoint plane and the profile where the profile is ahead of it. That single path is the strand's visible outline with the new end.
  2. Inner fill. The outer footprint inset by stroke_width along the long edges and by the side-line thickness along the profile (the two are equal unless the dialog changed the thickness). Along the long edges this is identical to today's fill stroker; around the new end it gives the uniform outline you see in the pictures. With the side line hidden the profile carries no band at all, so the fill reaches the edge, which is what hiding the line does today.
  3. Side-line band. The part of that inset ring that runs along the profile. It is filled in the side-line colour and thickness instead of being a separate drawLine, so it bends with a rounded end and meets the corners cleanly.
  4. Shadow. The outer footprint offset outward by the shadow extension (union of the path with its own outline stroked at twice the extension). The existing fade loop, which strokes the outline with growing pen widths, then works unchanged.

The default is pixel-identical to today. With Straight, 0° and 0 px the profile sits at x = stroke_width: the outer footprint is the flat cap plus the old side-line strip, the inset fill ends at the endpoint plane, and the band is exactly the old stroke_width × full-width line. Strands with no style set keep running the current code path, so nothing changes for existing projects.

Two things the prototype had to learn, worth keeping: the extension region is built directly as a polygon (one per run of the profile ahead of the endpoint), not as a box minus the cut, because Qt's path clipper mis-handles a box minus an arc; and where a tilted cut leaves the strand's width (a curved body bulges past it right behind the endpoint), the cut continues straight along its own line rather than turning square, which is what avoids a step or a wedge at the corners.

What moves together

The whole point of the feature is that the end is accurate everywhere, not just in the body paint. This is the list of places that read the end's geometry today and must read the styled footprint instead.

PieceTodayWith a styled end
Body stroke & fillTwo FlatCap strokers in Strand.draw, duplicated in _draw_direct and twice more in AttachedStrand.Draw the outer footprint in the stroke colour, the inner footprint in the strand colour. Put the cap construction in one helper the four draw bodies share.
Side lineupdate_side_line computes two points; drawLine with a stroke_width pen in the stroke colour.Fill the band path in the side-line colour and thickness. update_side_line keeps producing its two points (highlight, bounding rect and decoration path use them) but from the profile's corners.
Selection & hit-testingget_selection_path = flat body + end decoration; get_end_selection_path = circle around the endpoint ∩ selection path.Body selection path = outer footprint. The endpoint circle rule already clips to the footprint, so an extended end becomes clickable and a trimmed one stops being clickable, with no extra code.
Highlight_draw_unified_highlight widens the body and the side line by 10 px.Widen the outer footprint instead; the band is part of it.
Bounding rectBody rect ∪ side-line rects.Outer footprint rect, so an extended end is never clipped by the paint cache.
Shadow castbuild_shadow_geometry strokes the centre curve with FlatCap.Return the outer footprint (dilated by fixed_shadow_extension when non-zero). The transparent-cap circle subtraction stays as is.
Shadow receivebuild_rendered_geometry strokes the centre curve, unions caps and arrow.Start from the outer footprint, then union caps and arrow as today.
MasksThe five get_*_for_strand helpers in MaskedStrand stroke strand.get_path() and union in the elliptical caps.Ask the component for its footprint (inner or outer, with or without shadow margin) exactly the way _elliptical_caps_path is unioned in today. Because the mask is recomputed on every paint from the live components, the intersection then follows a trimmed, angled or extended end automatically. get_masked_shadow_path and draw_mask_strand_shadow take the same paths. Deletion rectangles and the edited centre point are untouched.
Dash extension & small arrowStart at the endpoint along the tangent.Start at the profile's farthest point, so they never sit on top of an extended cap and do not float away from a trimmed one.
Attaching later—If that end later gets a circle (has_circles becomes true), the circle cap wins and the style goes dormant, exactly like end_line_visible today; if the end becomes free again the style comes back. The endpoint never moved, so attach mode, move mode and snapping are unaffected.
Save / loadPer-end flags in serialize_strand and three deserialize blocks.Add end_styles to the serializer and to all three deserialize blocks. Old files have no key, which reads as "no style" (today's look).
Undo / redoAttribute diff list in undo_redo_manager.Add end_styles to the diff list; the dialog saves one strand.end_style state on OK.
Duplicate / copyGroup duplication copies strand properties; the clipboard copies six essentials.Group duplication copies end_styles. Clipboard: not copied, consistent with every other per-end flag.
Hidden, shadow-only, lockedFlags checked in the draw bodies.Unchanged. A shadow-only layer casts the styled shadow; a hidden layer casts none.

Data & wording

Per-end style on the strand

One list parallel to has_circles: end_styles = [start, end], each entry None (today's look, fast path) or a small record.

end_styles = [None, {
    "shape":      "pointed",   # straight | angled | rounded | pointed | notched | concave
    "tilt":       15.0,        # degrees, -60 .. 60, 0 = square to the strand
    "depth":      0.5,         # 0 .. 1, share of the strand width (ignored by straight/angled)
    "offset":     0.0,         # px along the tangent, negative trims
    "line_width": None,        # px, None = stroke_width
    "line_color": None,        # QColor, None = stroke_color
}]
# side-line visibility stays in start_line_visible / end_line_visible

Strand grows three read-only helpers that everything above calls: get_footprint_path(inner=False) for the whole strand with both ends applied, get_end_band_path(side), and get_end_profile_extent(side) (the farthest point, for the dash and arrow). Cache the result per strand and invalidate in update_shape, the same place the side-line points are refreshed.

Rules & edge cases

  • The endpoint is sacred. Extend / Trim moves the edge, never strand.end. Attach mode, move mode, snapping, angle adjust and the mask centre logic all key off the endpoint and keep working.
  • Tilt is capped at ±60° and Trim at half the width, so a cut can never run back along the strand or leave a sliver.
  • Frame follows the curve. The profile lives in the tangent frame at the end and is recomputed whenever the curve changes, so dragging a control point re-aims the cut with the strand.
  • Circle beats style. An end that is attached, or closed with Close the Knot, draws its circle cap and ignores its style until it is free again. The menu only offers the row for free ends in the first place.
  • Attached strands can style their end only; masked layers get no row, but their two components' styled ends shape the mask.
  • Side line off still cuts the body to the profile; only the band is skipped. Matches how Hide End Line leaves the flat cap in place today.
  • Elliptical junction caps (Match connected strand) apply to attached ends and never conflict with this, which applies to free ends.
  • Old files load unchanged: no end_styles key means [None, None].

Two calls to confirm before building. (1) The dialog previews live on the canvas (like the shadow editor) rather than only inside the dialog (like the width dialog); this makes Cancel a real restore, so the opening snapshot must include both ends' styles and the side-line flags. (2) Extend / Trim is in pixels; the width dialog thinks in grid squares (27 px). Pixels are more useful at this scale, but a grid-squares variant would be a one-line change.

Reproducing the pictures: docs/stylize_end_side_feature/tools/end_styles.py is the geometry prototype (the functions profile_points and styled_end_geometry are the algorithm described above, running against the real Strand), render_menu.py screenshots the app's real context menu with the row injected, and render_dialog.py builds the Qt dialog mockup. All three run offscreen with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and change nothing in the app.
